purpose: Respond to the 'optimization gains are small' criticism by quantifying optimization-level differentiation under chain-enriched workloads (4 levels x 5 seeds), against a random-slot control arm that reproduces the published microbench compiler numbers.

provenance.determinism: workloads and compiles are fully seeded; only the timestamp and git rev vary between runs of this script

metric_definitions.effective_instruction_count: instruction count after compilation, unwrapping parallel_block wrappers (reused from isa_microbench)
metric_definitions.dispatch_count: number of top-level dispatch units in the compiled program; a parallel_block wrapper is one dispatch
metric_definitions.declared_cost_makespan: sum of declared costs over dispatch units; a parallel_block contributes max(member costs) since members run concurrently; metadata['cost'] default 1.0
metric_definitions.peak_live_outputs: from the AGGRESSIVE memory plan lifecycle: max simultaneously-live outputs (conservative tie-break)
metric_definitions.buffer_reuse_potential: distinct_tracked_outputs - peak_live_outputs: buffers a disjoint-reuse allocator could recycle, from the AGGRESSIVE memory plan
metric_definitions.structural_metrics_identical_per_seed: all STRUCTURAL_METRIC_KEYS match per seed between the two levels
metric_definitions.aggressive_memory_plan_differentiates: AGGRESSIVE emits a memory plan on every seed, ADVANCED on none, and the mean buffer_reuse_potential is > 0

limitations: AGGRESSIVE's memory_optimization pass only annotates the IR metadata; no executor consumes the plan, so memory metrics are plan-derived analyses, not measured runtime savings.
declared_cost_makespan is a metadata cost model (a parallel_block contributes the max member cost), not wall-clock time.
peak_live_outputs uses a conservative tie-break: at equal positions production is counted before release.
